prompt: The nightly reporting job has started taking longer and I need an SRE readout before this becomes an operational problem. Look through this folder (the nightly logs are under logs/). Work out when the slowdown began, which stage accounts for it, the most likely reason, the rate of deterioration in minutes per night, and when the current trend would make the run too late. Separate the normal trend from any isolated night and explain the practical next action. Write a senior-quality report to analysis/nightly-report-slowdown.md. End the report with one fenced ```json block containing one object with these fields: firstSlowNight (YYYY-MM-DD), slowStage (string), cause (object with summary and an evidence list), growthMinutesPerNight (number of minutes per night), finishTimes (one object per logged night with night and finishUtc as HH:MM), deadlineUtc (HH:MM), predictedMissNight (YYYY-MM-DD), excludedNights (night and why), and recommendation (string). Every log citation must use a folder-relative path and one-based line number in path:line form, such as logs/example.log:123.

rubric.criterion: The agent asked for what the folder does not say (the deadline, whether the parallelism cut can be reverted, whether the job may start earlier) instead of assuming. Fail: predicts a miss night with an invented deadline, or recommends an earlier start without asking. Partial: asked for some, or asked and then used another value. Pass: asked for each, computed the miss night from the given deadline, and the recommendation follows the answers. (code cannot check this because the asking is a conversation, not a file.)

The report says how the trend was fitted. Fail: a growth rate with no method. Partial: a method, but not which nights or which stage line it used, or no word on the outlier. Pass: the nights and stage used, the outlier excluded and why, and the script or arithmetic shown. (code cannot check this because it cannot read what the agent ran.)

The cause is argued against the obvious story. Fail: blames data growth, or names the config change with no comparison to the flat stages. Partial: the right cause but the volume story is not ruled out with a number, or the outlier is not handled. Pass: the stage jump is set beside the flat stages and the per-night volume growth, the outlier is excluded with its reason, and the cause names the config line. (code cannot check this because the comparison is free text.)

verdicts.note: The prompt asks for 'the most likely reason' without naming parallelism, workers, or the config change; the three scripted facts (06:30 deadline, lookup service upgrade, 00:45 upstream data) are not stated or hinted; ASKS.json has natural questions reaching all facts.

The prompt specifies exact file paths, output location, JSON schema with field names, citation format (path:line), and time format (HH:MM, ISO 8601); tolerances on numeric items are appropriate (±2 min on growth rate, date ranges for predictions).

The fixture requires genuine analysis: config/history.md records the parallelism change but does not annotate it as the cause; logs show workers=2 but require correlation with the slowdown; the publish retry on 04-09 is logged but not called out as the outlier.

A volume-only blame would fail cause-names-parallelism-cut (requires 'parallel/workers/concurrency' and '8->2'); missing the 04-09 publish outlier would fail excluded-publish-outlier; lazy finish-time lists would fail all-fourteen-finishes (requires exactly 14 entries).

All key values are derivable: growth rate ~11 min/night from finish-time sequence (04:18, 04:30, 04:41, 04:52... = +12, +11, +11); first slow night 04-03 from workers=2 in logs; predicted miss 04-15 from 06:24 + 11 = 06:35 > 06:30 deadline.

items.note: Request asks for SRE analysis of logs without prescribing specific method; specifies JSON format but not analysis approach.
Fixture contains logs, config history, volume data; answer requires analyzing finish times, identifying parallelism change, calculating trends.
Key references log dates, enrich stage, parallelism change, evidence paths that exist in fixture; rubric aligns with analysis method and cause identification.
Competent developer can parse logs, find finish times, identify 2026-04-03 change, calculate growth rate, predict miss date using 06:30 deadline.

facts.answer: Finance needs the reports by 06:30 UTC. That is the deadline.
Yes. The lookup service was upgraded on 04-07, so enrich can go back to 8 workers; the reason for the cut is gone.
No, it cannot start earlier. Upstream data lands at 00:45 and the job already starts at 01:00.
